page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-48xCPU-512GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 48 physical cores and 48 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared, and the processor includes 64 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 10.67 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance measured by stress-ng falls into the bottom 10%, and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show average performance. However, multi-threaded operations leverage the 48-core architecture effectively, with bzip3 multi-threaded decompression and Passmark CPU metrics scoring in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth for both small and large blocks remains in the average tier, as does the Passmark memory score. Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput also perform within the middle 50% range.

The primary tradeoff of this server is its shared CPU allocation and low single-core speed, which limits its suitability for latency-sensitive or single-threaded workloads. For example, text generation using a medium 7B LLM model is poor, placing in the bottom 10%. Conversely, the large 512.0 GB memory capacity and strong multi-core performance make it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-intensive, highly parallelized tasks. It is suited for large-scale database operations, multi-threaded data processing, and memory-heavy web serving workloads that do not require local NVMe storage.
